newsitem.title: USA: US Sen Daschle accuses Republicans of budget stall.
newsitem.headline: US Sen Daschle accuses Republicans of budget stall.

text.p: Senate Democratic Leader Tom Daschle and a group of leading Democrats accused Republicans on Thursday of stalling on the budget talks and failing to come up with their own version.
"The Republicans don't have a plan, they only appear to want to criticize the Democrats' plan," Daschle told a news conference. "Obviously, we're ready to go to work."

He said that Republicans had found a number of excuses for not moving ahead on talks, the latest being discussion on what to do about making the Consumer Price Index more accurate, a move that could potentially cut government outlays substantially.

"Since there isn't a consensus (on what to do), I don't understand why we should use that as a reason not to get to our work and that in essence is what the Republicans are saying," he told reporters.
The Democratic senators noted that the Clinton's budget does not include any gain from a reduction in the level of the CPI.

A cut in the CPI, which is estimated by an independent commission to overstate inflation by 1.1 percent, would be one way to cut the deficit, because increases in annual government programs are keyed to it.
Daschle was joined by Frank Lautenberg of New Jersey, Ernest Hollings of South Carolina, Barbara Boxer of California, and Ron Wyden of Oregon.
